lessons.title: Solution Generation & FMEA
lessons.content_md:
# Solution Generation & FMEA

## Generating Solutions

After identifying root causes, brainstorm solutions using:

### Brainstorming Rules
1. No criticism during idea generation
2. Build on others' ideas
3. Encourage wild ideas
4. Go for quantity first, quality later

### Solution Selection Matrix

| Solution | Impact (1-5) | Feasibility (1-5) | Cost (1-5) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add dropdown validation | 5 | 4 | 5 | 14 |
| Hire more QA staff | 3 | 2 | 1 | 6 |
| Redesign survey form | 4 | 3 | 3 | 10 |
| Mobile data collection | 5 | 3 | 2 | 10 |

## FMEA — Failure Mode and Effects Analysis

FMEA proactively identifies what could go wrong with your solution:

| Failure Mode | Severity (1-10) | Occurrence (1-10) | Detection (1-10) | RPN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Users bypass validation | 7 | 4 | 3 | 84 |
| System crashes under load | 9 | 2 | 5 | 90 |
| Training not completed | 6 | 5 | 4 | 120 |

**RPN** = Severity × Occurrence × Detection

Prioritize actions for highest RPN items first.

## Pilot Planning

1. Select a representative pilot group (1-2 districts)
2. Define success criteria before starting
3. Run for a fixed duration (4-6 weeks)
4. Compare pilot results against baseline
5. Gather feedback from pilot participants

# Reflection Quiz

Test your understanding of the Design/Improve phase.

quiz_data.question: What does RPN stand for in FMEA?
What is the purpose of a pilot test?
options: Validate the solution on a small scale before full rollout
